questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose it as I Melbourne would be a cool city to live in, with a lot of culture, and Australia is a very safe country, which is far away and different but the culture is still relatively similar to Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, University of Melbourne sends a lot of information and they reply to emails quickly if you have any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Free ride to accommodation from the airport. And it's easy to get assistance from the University if you have any questions in the orientation weeks.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It's not easy to find accommodation in Melbourne, as there is a housing crisis. If you are willing to pay a lot, the student housing on Uni is nice, but it's veeery expensive, so I chose to find something elsewhere through the facebook group Fairy Floss. I would definitely reccommend looking for a place in the areas; Fitzroy, Carlton, Richmond or Brunswick, as these are the nicest with the most young people and students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great, it's just difficult to find a place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They email you all the information you need, and the system is easy to navigate.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Theres multiple ways to reach out, and they respond quickly to emails and so on.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy and I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes some time to prepare and register, but I think it does no matter where you're going, and I think University of Melbourne has a pretty smooth process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 MA classes and 1 BA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was very similar, we often had 1 hour lecture and then 2 hours tutorials. However, I had no exams at all, I only had a lot of assignments throughout the semester, which all counted towards your grade, so that can be a bit stressful. Some classes have exams, depends on which ones you choose.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and Health
Population Mental Health
Adolescent Sexuality and Sexual Health
Australian Surfing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Gender and Health, gave me a lot of new insights
Population Mental Health was very basic public health
Adolescent Sexuality and Sexual Health was very interesting, but it was unfortunately an online class. I think I would rather have had an on campus class.
Australian Surfing was very unserious and a nice break.
I would reccommend to look into whether the courses have exams or only assignments, I found it really nice not to have exams. Also look at whether the courses have mandatory attendance, a lot of them don't.

questions.answer: Student visa is very expensive, some universities allow you to get the holiday visa instead. Maybe price of visa will drop in the future because of the new deal between EU and Australia

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive, similar to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and events going on all the time

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate a lot, but there are a lot of clubs at uni that you can be a part of.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went travelling around Australia to see other places a lot, there are som much beautiful nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, generally Australians are very open and easy to talk to, and Melbourne is a very multicultural city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are lots of international students, and they are all interested in making friends, so don't be shy :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very open, welcoming, helpful and easy to talk to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't stress about picking the right courses, it's very easy to change course in the beginning of the semester if you want to.
2. Prioritise living in a nice neighbourhood
3. Don't take uni to seriously, have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet a lot of nice people from different places around the world and seeing a lot of beatiful australian culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
